note: Braids' TIMBRE is the breath-noise depth and its COLOR is the body filter's corner, so p1 maps to the engine's TIMBRE and p2 to its HARMONICS, both 1:1. MORPH and MACRO sit at noon in every case, where Blow is 0.8 and Reed is 0.69995 -- the two constants the module welds.
whyMostCasesAreTriggered: BLOWN is a noise-driven chaotic self-oscillator, and which limit cycle it settles into depends on the noise realisation. Measured by rendering the MODULE against ITSELF from twenty different RNG seeds (190 pairs), held and untriggered for 3 s at MIDI 45: at COLOR noon the AC RMS spreads 2.59 dB and the pairwise spectral difference reaches 8.49 dB; at COLOR 0 it spreads 10.49 dB and 9.86 dB. Longer renders make it worse, not better -- at 20 s one pair reads 2.05 dB and 8.74 dB -- because the model wanders rather than averaging. So a HELD A/B of this model cannot resolve anything finer than about 9 dB, no matter how correct the port is; a tolerance tighter than that would fail a bit-exact port, and one that loose is not a test. Retriggering fixes it. A strike flushes the bore and nothing else (digital_oscillator.cc:1311-1314), so both sides then average over many independent settlings, and the same twenty-seed module-against-itself measurement at triggerHz 8 reads at most 1.18 dB of AC RMS spread and 0.69 dB of spectral difference. The parameter-axis cases are therefore triggered and hold the guide's ordinary tolerances; two held cases are kept to record the phenomenon, with tolerances taken from that measurement rather than from what the port happens to do.
whereTheCentsToleranceIsOmitted: ab_engine's f0 estimator is a 0.25 s autocorrelation with a 0.25 correlation floor and a 2000 Hz ceiling. Two of these cases defeat it, and the evidence is that they defeat the MODULE, not the port: across the twenty reference seeds the estimator's own reading spans 5019 cents at body-dark and 7420 cents at the low note, pinning at the 2000 Hz f_max on some seeds. body-dark is a 112 Hz-cornered tone with almost nothing above the fundamental to correlate; the low note is 27.5 Hz, four cycles per 0.25 s window. Those two cases therefore declare no cents tolerance, and low-sustained -- where the module's own reading spans 0.05 cents -- carries the low-octave pitch check instead. Everywhere else the module's own spread is under 0.5 cents and a 1.0 cent tolerance is real.

cases.name: Body filter at its floor
cases.toleranceNote: No cents tolerance -- see whereTheCentsToleranceIsOmitted. The level and spectrum tolerances are the ordinary ones and the port meets them.

cases.name: Body filter inside its live range at this note
cases.toleranceNote: COLOR 0.4 is inside the range that does anything at MIDI 45. Verified by rendering the module: COLOR 0.0, 0.10, 0.14, 0.15 and 0.156 come out bit-identical to each other and 0.157 differs, as do 0.766, 0.78, 0.80 and 1.0 while 0.75 differs, because the filter index stays clamped at 0 below COLOR 0.1563 (the raw sum crosses zero at 0.1484, but the >> 7 holds the index at 0 until it reaches 128) and the table saturates at entry 79 above COLOR 0.766.

cases.name: Two octaves down, a long bore
cases.toleranceNote: Triggered at 2 Hz, not 8, so each strike gets enough cycles of a 27.5 Hz bore to settle. No cents tolerance -- see whereTheCentsToleranceIsOmitted.

cases.name: The low bore held, where its pitch is measurable
cases.toleranceNote: Held, so the level and spectrum tolerances come from the module against itself at this note: 2.23 dB of AC RMS spread and at most 4.32 dB of spectral difference across twenty seeds. The cents tolerance is the tight one, because f0 IS stable here on both sides -- the module's own reading spans 0.05 cents.

cases.name: Two octaves up, where the body filter is already open
TIMBRE swept across the whole knob
COLOR swept across the whole knob
Held, untriggered, as the module is normally played
cases.toleranceNote: Deliberately loose, and taken from the module against itself rather than from the port: 2.59 dB of AC RMS spread and up to 8.49 dB of pairwise spectral difference across twenty noise seeds. Anything tighter would fail a bit-exact port. Kept because the held tone is how the module is actually played, and because a change that broke it badly would still show here -- the port reads 0.0 to 1.3 dB and 2.7 to 6.3 dB depending on its own seed. The worst corner is worse still and is not given a case: held at COLOR 0, twenty module renders span 10.49 dB of AC RMS and 9.86 dB of spectral difference, which is no longer a test of anything. That corner is covered sharply by the triggered body-dark case instead.
